content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some candidate building blocks: need to break into simpler pieces.

Target has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). Actually the amide is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) i.e., an aniline with an amide linking to the double bond.

Simplify: Could be assembled via sulfonyl chloride coupling of an aniline with sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl). Also amide formation via coupling of aniline with acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl acid + coupling). So retrosynthesis: disconnection 1: sulfonamide formation between aniline (para-methyl phenyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-bromophenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl part is attached to a phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which also bears the unsaturated amide side chain. So we could have sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-aryl (aryl = 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl). Then react with para-methyl aniline (4-methyl aniline) to give sulfonamide.

Thus step 1: sulfonamide formation.

Step 2: synthesis of the sulfonyl chloride precursor: from the aryl sulfonic acid (aryl-SO3H) chlorination (SO3H to SO2Cl). Could get aryl sulfonyl chloride commercially? Maybe not. Could instead start from aryl sulfonic acid (aryl-SO3H) which may be commercially available. Search for "ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Br)cc1" we have price 115 for 250 mg. That's a sulfonyl chloride with bromophenyl. Our aryl is phenyl with a side chain (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). That is not commercially available likely. So we need to construct that aryl sulfonyl chloride via sulfonation of the aryl (e.g., bromobenzene sulfonation) then substitution? But we need the side chain attached to the aryl before sulfonylation? Sulfonation is electrophilic aromatic substitution; the side chain may be deactivating. Might be okay.

Alternative route: first form the amide side chain on a phenyl ring, then sulfonylate that phenyl, then convert to sulfonyl chloride, then couple with aniline.

Thus steps: 1) Start from 4-bromoaniline? Actually we need phenyl with side chain: 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl. Could be made via Heck coupling of 4-bromoaniline with acrylamide? Or via condensation of 4-aminobenzaldehyde with something? The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (trans). That's a cinnamamide attached to an aniline (para). So we could start from 4-iodoaniline (or 4-bromoaniline) and do a Heck coupling with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Acrylamide is commercially available? Search.
